title: Hybrid psychosomatic rehabilitation - manualization and evaluation
summary:
The study "HypeR-ME" evaluates a psychosomatic hybrid rehabilitation program that includes a digital "bridge week" at home, following a 4-week inpatient rehabilitation. The concept of hybrid rehab is based on the idea that during this digital bridge week, participants can more easily integrate what they have learned during rehabilitation into their daily life and professional environment, while also facilitating the more reliable transfer of therapeutic processes into their home setting.
In a preliminary study ("Hybrid-Reha", 2021-2024), the feasibility, acceptance, and satisfaction with the concept were assessed and documented.
The evaluation study will investigate the benefits and effectiveness of psychosomatic hybrid rehabilitation compared to traditional psychosomatic rehabilitation. It will also track changes in participation, as well as in various health- and work-related parameters, over time as part of a controlled longitudinal study.

interventions.name: psychosomatic Hybrid rehabilitation (4-week inpatient phase followed by a therapeutically supported bridge week in the home environment, including digital therapy sessions and self-administered exercises)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnoses: F3 - F6; employed subject to social insurance contributions; unemployed, temporary disability pension; access to a digital device/Internet connection; cognitive, communicative, emotional and physical suitability as well as socio-medical suitability; informed consent to participate in the study; funding agencies: DRV Bund, DRV Rheinland and DRV KBS
Exclusion criteria:
Diagnoses: F0, F1 and F2; application for reduced earning capacity pension/retired; lack of technical infrastructure; lack of technical skills; lack of consent
